config.title: Container queries

intro.title: Container queries
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a responsive card component that adapts its layout based on the size of its container, not just the viewport. You will learn the core concept of container queries, a modern CSS feature that allows elements to respond to their parent container's dimensions. The main technologies involved are CSS container queries, using properties like container-type and container-name, and the @container rule. This approach provides more flexible and modular responsive design compared to traditional media queries.
intro.usecase: Container queries solve a common lesson in modern web development: components that need to adapt their layout based on their available space, not just the viewport. You'll see this in product dashboards where sidebar panels, data cards, and metric widgets resize intelligently as users drag divider handles or collapse navigation menus. News websites use container queries for article grids that flow differently in main content areas versus narrower sidebars. E-commerce sites apply them to product cards that display more details when placed in wide containers but show compact versions in filtered result lists. This allows developers to create truly reusable components that work anywhere in the interface without media query duplication.

objectives: Apply the container-type property to designate an element as a query container.
Construct a container query using the @container rule to target a specific container.
Configure responsive typography by adjusting font-size within a container query.
Manipulate layout properties like padding and margin based on container dimensions.
Integrate container queries with flexbox or grid to create adaptive component layouts.
Initialize a container query that modifies element colors when the container width changes.
Implement a container query to control the visibility or display of child elements.

steps.title: Create a basic HTML structure for container queries
steps.instruction:
Create a simple HTML structure with a container element and content inside it. Use a
with class 'container' and a

element inside with some text.
steps.hint: Start with a container div that will be the parent element. Inside it, add a paragraph element with any text content.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a basic HTML structure with a container element that can be targeted with container queries.
successCriteria: A container div with class 'container' exists and contains a paragraph element with text content.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you have a container div with class 'container' and a paragraph element inside it with some text.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create a container div with class 'container' and add a paragraph element inside it with some text content.

steps.title: Add basic styling to the container and content
steps.instruction: Add CSS rules to style the container with a light gray background, padding, and a border, and style the paragraph with a dark text color and font size.
steps.hint: Use the class selector .container for the container and .container p for the paragraph inside it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The container will have a light gray background with padding and a border, and the paragraph inside will have dark text with a readable font size.
successCriteria: CSS rules are added for .container with background-color, padding, and border properties, and for .container p with color and font-size properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some styling, but make sure to include all the required properties: background-color, padding, and border for the container, and color and font-size for the paragraph inside it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The styling is missing or incorrect. Please add CSS rules for the .container class and the .container p selector with the specified properties.

steps.title: Define the container type
steps.instruction: Add the container-type property to the .container rule to make it queryable. Set it to inline-size.
steps.hint: Use the container-type property with the value inline-size to enable container queries based on width.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .container rule now has container-type: inline-size; applied, making it a queryable container.
successCriteria: The .container selector includes the container-type property set to inline-size.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added container-type: inline-size; to the .container rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The container type wasn't properly defined. Add container-type: inline-size; to the .container rule to enable container queries.

steps.title: Add a container name for targeting
steps.instruction: Add a container-name property to the .container rule to give it a specific name for targeting in container queries.
steps.hint: Use the container-name property with a descriptive name like 'card' or 'widget'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The container will have a specific name that can be referenced in container queries.
successCriteria: The .container rule includes a container-name property with a valid name.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the container-name property is correctly spelled and has a value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The container-name property is missing or incorrect. Check the syntax and try again.

steps.title: Create your first container query
steps.instruction: Add a container query rule that changes the paragraph's text color to blue when the container width is at least 400px.
steps.hint: Use @container with a min-width condition. The syntax is similar to media queries but targets the container instead of the viewport.
steps.expectedOutcome: The paragraph text will turn blue when the container width reaches 400px or more.
successCriteria: A @container rule with (min-width: 400px) is added and changes the paragraph's color to blue.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your container query uses the correct syntax: @container (min-width: 400px) { ... } and targets the paragraph inside.
steps.feedbackWrong: The container query is missing or incorrect. Remember to use @container with a min-width condition and apply a color style to the paragraph.

steps.title: Apply styles inside the container query
steps.instruction: Inside your existing @container rule, add CSS declarations to change the paragraph's appearance when the container is at least 400px wide. Specifically, set the paragraph's font-size to 1.5rem and its color to darkblue.
steps.hint: Add the CSS rules directly inside the @container rule block you created in the previous step. Use the selector .content p to target the paragraph.
steps.expectedOutcome: The container query now contains CSS rules that will change the paragraph's appearance when the container width reaches 400px.
successCriteria: The @container rule contains the selector .content p with font-size: 1.5rem and color: darkblue declarations.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added both the font-size and color declarations inside the @container rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The container query should contain CSS rules that target the paragraph element and change its font-size and color when the container reaches 400px width.

steps.title: Create multiple container query breakpoints
steps.instruction: Add a second @container rule with a different min-width condition (e.g., 600px) below your existing container query.
steps.hint: You can add multiple @container rules to create different style changes at different container sizes. Place the new rule after your existing one.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have two @container rules with different min-width conditions, enabling progressive style changes as the container grows.
successCriteria: A second @container rule with a different min-width condition (e.g., 600px) is added below the first one.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a second rule, but check that it uses a different min-width condition (like 600px) and is placed after the first @container rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The second container query is missing or incorrect. Add a new @container rule with a different min-width condition below the existing one.

steps.title: Use container query units (cqw, cqh)
steps.instruction: In the existing container query for min-width: 400px, replace the absolute pixel units in the font-size and padding properties with container query width (cqw) and container query height (cqh) units.
steps.hint: Instead of using px values, try using cqw for width-based sizing and cqh for height-based sizing. For example, font-size: 5cqw;
steps.expectedOutcome: The container query styles will now use container-relative units that scale with the container's dimensions instead of fixed pixel values.
successCriteria: The container query for min-width: 400px contains at least one property using cqw or cqh units.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using cqw or cqh units instead of px in the container query styles.
steps.feedbackWrong: The container query still uses absolute pixel units. Try replacing px values with cqw or cqh units inside the @container block.

steps.title: Create a nested container query scenario
steps.instruction: Add a nested container inside your main container and apply container queries to it
steps.hint: Create a new div with a class like 'nested-container' inside the existing .container div, then define container properties and queries for this nested element.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a nested container inside your main container with its own container properties and responsive styles.
successCriteria: A nested container element is created with container-type and container-name properties, and a container query targeting that nested container is defined.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've defined both the nested container element and a container query that specifically targets it using its container name.
steps.feedbackWrong: The nested container scenario isn't complete yet. You need to add a nested container element, define its container properties, and create a container query that targets it.

steps.title: Test and refine the container query implementation
steps.instruction: Add a final container query breakpoint for when the container width is at least 800px, and inside it, set the paragraph text color to darkgreen.
steps.hint: Use @container with (min-width: 800px) and target the paragraph inside the container.
steps.expectedOutcome: The paragraph text color changes to darkgreen when the container width reaches 800px or more.
successCriteria: A container query for (min-width: 800px) is added and sets the paragraph text color to darkgreen.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the container query targets the paragraph and sets the text color to darkgreen.
steps.feedbackWrong: The container query for 800px breakpoint is missing or incorrect. Remember to use @container (min-width: 800px) and set the paragraph text color to darkgreen.
